newsitem.title: USA: Miami Dolphins seek Florida sales tax rebate.
newsitem.headline: Miami Dolphins seek Florida sales tax rebate.

text.p: A bill before the Florida Legislature would give the Miami Dolphins up to $60 million of sales tax rebates to fund improvements at Pro Player Stadium.
The proposal (HB1145 and SB1438) was sponosred by Rep. John Thrasher, R-Orange Park, and Sen. Ron Silver, D-North Miami Beach.
Other professional sports teams in Florida already receive the sales tax rebate under a 1988 law designed to help bring new teams to Florida.

The Dolphins were well established at the time and were not eligible. But the law has already been amended to extend the tax break to the long-established Tampa Bay Buccaneers and to benefit existing facilities for baseball spring training.

the Dolphins are owned by Wayne Huizenga, who also owns the Florida Marlins baseball team. Huizenga received the tax break for Pro Player Stadium once before, to convert the football stadium for major league baseball.
Huizenga associates said the stadium, formerly known Joe Robbie Stadium, needs additional improvements before hosting the 1999 Super Bowl.
